```text
  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
Archer::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Generates all candidate moves for an Archer piece from a given source square, applying orthogonal movement and Chinese Cannon-style capture mechanics.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: game.getPiece(place), directional iteration logic.
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, Color
Input: game (current game state containing board and configuration), source (Place where the Archer stands)
Output: List<Move> containing all geometrically valid orthogonal moves and valid captures according to Archer mechanics.
Pre-condition: source is a valid Place on the board and contains an Archer piece belonging to the active player.
Post-condition: Returns a list of Move objects representing all possible destinations reachable by the Archer without violating piece-specific movement constraints. Global and ownership rules are applied later by the validation pipeline.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Evaluates post-move win conditions based on game rules and current board state.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Central place reference, piece counting, score comparison, turn tracking.
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Configuration, Color
Input: lastPlayer (Player who just moved), lastPiece (Piece moved), lastMove (Move executed)
Output: Player (the winning player) or null if game continues.
Pre-condition: Board state reflects the position after executing lastMove.
Post-condition: Determines game outcome per specification. Does not modify board or scores.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Orchestrates the complete move generation and validation pipeline for a given player, returning all legally executable moves.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Board traversal, rule chaining, polymorphic piece move generation.
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Rule, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Place
Input: player (Player whose turn it is)
Output: List<Move> containing all moves that pass the full validation pipeline.
Pre-condition: player is registered in the game and corresponds to currentPlayer. Board state is consistent.
Post-condition: Returns a filtered list of moves. The board state and scores remain completely unchanged.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Calculates and applies the Manhattan distance score increase for a successful move.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Coordinate arithmetic, score accumulation.
Related Classes: Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player whose score is updated), piece (Piece that moved, context only), move (Move executed)
Output: void
Pre-condition: move was successfully executed and validated.
Post-condition: player's score is increased by exactly the Manhattan distance between source and destination coordinates.

JesonMor::start
Summary: Initializes the game from Configuration and runs the core turn-based loop until a winner is determined.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Game state initialization, turn switching, UI refresh, pipeline orchestration.
Related Classes: Game, Player, Move, Configuration, Piece, JesonMor
Input: none
Output: Player (the winner of the match)
Pre-condition: A valid Configuration object has been passed to constructor/init.
Post-condition: Game loop terminates. Board reflects final state. Winner is returned. All side effects (scores, board updates) are committed.

JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a validated move by relocating the piece on the internal board representation and updating the turn counter.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Board state mutation via Game.getPiece/setPiece contract, turn counter increment.
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input: move (Move object specifying source and destination)
Output: void
Pre-condition: move has passed all validation rules; source contains a piece belonging to currentPlayer.
Post-condition: Board state updated: piece moved to destination, source square cleared. Turn counter incremented. Scores and win status unchanged (handled by other methods).

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Evaluates post-move win conditions based on game rules and current board state.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Central place reference, piece counting, score comparison, turn tracking.
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Configuration, Color
Input: lastPlayer (Player who just moved), lastPiece (Piece moved), lastMove (Move executed)
Output: Player (the winning player) or null if game continues.
Pre-condition: Board state reflects the position after executing lastMove.
Post-condition: Determines game outcome per specification. Does not modify board or scores.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Orchestrates the complete move generation and validation pipeline for a given player, returning all legally executable moves.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Board traversal, rule chaining, polymorphic piece move generation.
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Rule, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Place
Input: player (Player whose turn it is)
Output: List<Move> containing all moves that pass the full validation pipeline.
Pre-condition: player is registered in the game and corresponds to currentPlayer. Board state is consistent.
Post-condition: Returns a filtered list of moves. The board state and scores remain completely unchanged.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Calculates and applies the Manhattan distance score increase for a successful move.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Coordinate arithmetic, score accumulation.
Related Classes: Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player whose score is updated), piece (Piece that moved, context only), move (Move executed)
Output: void
Pre-condition: move was successfully executed and validated.
Post-condition: player's score is increased by exactly the Manhattan distance between source and destination coordinates.

JesonMor::start
Summary: Initializes the game from Configuration and runs the core turn-based loop until a winner is determined.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Game state initialization, turn switching, UI refresh, pipeline orchestration.
Related Classes: Game, Player, Move, Configuration, Piece, JesonMor
Input: none
Output: Player (the winner of the match)
Pre-condition: A valid Configuration object has been passed to constructor/init.
Post-condition: Game loop terminates. Board reflects final state. Winner is returned. All side effects (scores, board updates) are committed.

JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a validated move by relocating the piece on the internal board representation and updating the turn counter.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Board state mutation via Game.getPiece/setPiece contract, turn counter increment.
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input: move (Move object specifying source and destination)
Output: void
Pre-condition: move has passed all validation rules; source contains a piece belonging to currentPlayer.
Post-condition: Board state updated: piece moved to destination, source square cleared. Turn counter incremented. Scores and win status unchanged (handled by other methods).

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

{org.eclipse.emf.ecore.impl.EOperationImpl@3a7c678b (name: validate) (ordered: true, unique: true, lowerBound: 0, upperBound: 1)=Summary: Validates the Chinese Chess-style blocking constraint specifically for Knight moves.
Algorithm: 
  1. Extract source and destination places from the move parameter.
  2. Calculate absolute differences: dx = |source.x - destination.x|, dy = |source.y - destination.y|.
  3. Determine the intermediate "hobble" square based on the primary direction of movement:
     - If dx == 2: blockingPlace = new Place((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y)
     - Else if dy == 2: blockingPlace = new Place(source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2)
  4. Query the board state using game.getPiece(blockingPlace).
  5. Return true if the returned piece is null (path unblocked), otherwise return false.
Related Features: Blocking coordinate derivation, piece presence check.
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
Input: game (provides board access via getPiece()), move (contains source and destination Place objects representing a Knight's candidate move)
Output: boolean (true if the intermediate blocking square is empty, false if occupied by any piece)
Pre-condition: The move originates from a Knight piece and satisfies the L-shaped displacement requirement (dx=1, dy=2 or dx=2, dy=1).
Post-condition: Board state remains completely unchanged. The method returns true if the hobble square is vacant, false if obstructed.}

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

```java
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
  {
```

```java
   *      - If dx == 2: blockingPlace = new Place((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y)

   *   4. Query the board state using game.getPiece(blockingPlace).
   *   5. Return true if the returned piece is null (path unblocked), otherwise return false.
   * Related Features: Blocking coordinate derivation, piece presence check.
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
   * Input: game (provides board access via getPiece()), move (contains source and destination Place objects representing a Knight's candidate move)
   * Output: boolean (true if the intermediate blocking square is empty, false if occupied by any piece)
   * Pre-condition: The move originates from a Knight piece and satisfies the L-shaped displacement requirement (dx=1, dy=2 or dx=2, dy=1).
   * Post-condition: Board state remains completely unchanged. The method returns true if the hobble square is vacant, false if obstructed.
```

      int dstY = move.getDestination().getY();

      // 1. Verify orthogonality
      if (!((srcX == dstX || srcY == dstY) && (srcX != dstX || srcY != dstY))) {

   * Related Features: Turn count tracking, central place reference, piece counting, win condition evaluation.
   * Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Configuration
   * Input: lastPlayer (Player who just moved), lastPiece (Piece moved), lastMove (Move executed)
   * Output: Player (the winning player) or null if game continues.
   * Pre-condition: Board state reflects the position after executing lastMove.
   * Post-condition: Determines game outcome per specification. Does not modify board or scores.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Player getWinner(final Player lastPlayer, final Piece lastPiece, final Move lastMove)
  {
    if (getNumMoves() < getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()) {
      return null;
    }
    if (lastPiece instanceof Knight && lastMove.getSource().equals(getConfiguration().getCentralPlace()) && !lastMove.getDestination().equals(getConfiguration().getCentralPlace())) {
      return lastPlayer;
    }
    int p0Count = 0;
    int p1Count = 0;
    for (Place place : getBoard()) {
      Piece piece = place.getOccupyingPiece();
      if (piece != null) {
        if (piece.getOwnerPlayer() == getPlayers().get(0)) {
          p0Count++;
        } else if (piece.getOwnerPlayer() == getPlayers().get(1)) {
          p1Count++;
        }
      }
    }
    if (p0Count > 0 && p1Count == 0) {
      return getPlayers().get(0);
    }
    if (p1Count > 0 && p0Count == 0) {
      return getPlayers().get(1);
    }
    return null;
  }

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Orchestrates the complete move generation and validation pipeline for a given player, returning all legally executable moves.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   1. Initialize List<Move> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
   *   2. Iterate over all valid board coordinates (x, y). If game.getPiece(x, y) exists and belongs to player, call piece.getAvailableMoves(game, new Place(x, y)) and add results to candidates.
   *   3. Initialize List<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
   *   4. For each move in candidates:
   *      a. Validate global rules sequentially: VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule. Skip if any returns false.
   *      b. Validate FirstNMovesProtectionRule. Skip if move captures a piece during the protection phase.
   *      c. Validate piece-specific rules: If move.piece instanceof Knight, run KnightMoveRule then KnightBlockRule. If instanceof Archer, run ArcherMoveRule. Skip if any fail.
   *      d. If all validations pass, add move to validMoves.
   *   5. Return validMoves.
   * Related Features: Board traversal, rule chaining, polymorphic piece move generation.
   * Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Rule, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Place
   * Input: player (Player whose turn it is)
   * Output: List<Move> containing all moves that pass the full validation pipeline.
   * Pre-condition: player is registered in the game and corresponds to currentPlayer. Board state is consistent.
   * Post-condition: Returns a filtered list of moves. The board state and scores remain completely unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Player player)
  {
    java.util.List<Move> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < super.getWidth(); x++) {
      for (int y = 0; y < super.getHeight(); y++) {
        Place pos = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
        pos.setX(x);
        pos.setY(y);
        Piece p = this.getPiece(pos);
        if (p != null && p.getOwnerPlayer() == player) {
          candidates.addAll(p.getAvailableMoves(this, pos));
        }
      }
    }
    
    java.util.List<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (Move move : candidates) {
      if (!VacantRule.check(this, move) || !NilMoveRule.check(this, move) || 
          !OutOfBoundaryRule.check(this, move) || !OccupiedRule.check(this, move)) {
        continue;
      }
      if (!FirstNMovesProtectionRule.check(this, move)) {
        continue;
      }
      if (move.getMovedPiece() instanceof Knight) {
        if (!KnightMoveRule.check(this, move) || !KnightBlockRule.check(this, move)) {
          continue;
        }
      } else if (move.getMovedPiece() instanceof Archer) {
        if (!ArcherMoveRule.check(this, move)) {
          continue;
        }
      }
      validMoves.add(move);
    }
    return new BasicEList<>(validMoves);
  }

```java
   * Summary: Validates the Chinese Chess-style blocking constraint specifically for Knight moves.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   1. Extract source and destination places from the move parameter.
   *   2. Calculate absolute differences: dx = |source.x - destination.x|, dy = |source.y - destination.y|.
   *   3. Determine the intermediate "hobble" square based on the primary direction of movement:
   *      - If dx == 2: blockingPlace = new Place((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y)
   *      - Else if dy == 2: blockingPlace = new Place(source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2)
   *   4. Query the board state using game.getPiece(blockingPlace).
   *   5. Return true if the returned piece is null (path unblocked), otherwise return false.
   * Related Features: Blocking coordinate derivation, piece presence check.
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
   * Input: game (provides board access via getPiece()), move (contains source and destination Place objects representing a Knight's candidate move)
   * Output: boolean (true if the intermediate blocking square is empty, false if occupied by any piece)
   * Pre-condition: The move originates from a Knight piece and satisfies the L-shaped displacement requirement (dx=1, dy=2 or dx=2, dy=1).
   * Post-condition: Board state remains completely unchanged. The method returns true if the hobble square is vacant, false if obstructed.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    
    int dx = Math.abs(source.getX() - destination.getX());
    int dy = Math.abs(source.getY() - destination.getY());
    
    Place blockingPlace;
    if (dx == 2) {
      blockingPlace = new Place((source.getX() + destination.getX()) / 2, source.getY());
    } else if (dy == 2) {
      blockingPlace = new Place(source.getX(), (source.getY() + destination.getY()) / 2);
    } else {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid Knight move coordinates");
    }
    
    return game.getPiece(blockingPlace) == null;
  }
```

```java
   *   3. Initialize List<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();

   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT

  {
    java.util.List<Move> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < this.getWidth(); x++) {
      for (int y = 0; y < this.getHeight(); y++) {
        Place pos = new Place(x, y);
        Piece p = this.getPiece(pos);
        if (p != null && p.getOwner() == player) {
          candidates.addAll(p.getAvailableMoves(this, pos));
        }
      }
    }
    
    java.util.List<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (Move move : candidates) {
      if (!VacantRule.isValid(move) || !NilMoveRule.isValid(move) || 
          !OutOfBoundaryRule.isValid(move) || !OccupiedRule.isValid(move)) {
        continue;
      }
      if (!FirstNMovesProtectionRule.isValid(move)) {
        continue;
      }
      if (move.getPiece() instanceof Knight) {
        if (!KnightMoveRule.isValid(move) || !KnightBlockRule.isValid(move)) {
          continue;
        }
      } else if (move.getPiece() instanceof Archer) {
        if (!ArcherMoveRule.isValid(move)) {
          continue;
        }
      }
      validMoves.add(move);
    }
    return new BasicEList<>(validMoves);
  }
```
